title: Compact deterministic liquid-crystal polarization controller with single-measurement direct control
authors: Ren-De Liu, Jie Wang, Dong-Dong Li, Xian-Chang Du, Dao-Zhong Xiao, shuai Li, Chuan-Yang Ding, Yan-Lin Tang, Yang Li, Sheng-Kai Liao, Teng-Yun Chen, Shi-Biao Tang
abstract: Polarization controllers (PCs) and their control algorithms are critical for compensating environmental disturbances and maintaining signal fidelity in polarization-sensitive photonic systems. However, existing controllers often involve trade-offs among key performance metrics, while associated control algorithms either converge inefficiently or require multiple state-of-polarization (SOP) measurements. This work presents a compact deterministic liquid-crystal polarization controller (LC-PC) with balanced overall performance, featuring low insertion loss (<1 dB), low driving voltage (<6 V), and full Poincaré sphere coverage. The device exhibits highly predictable and repeatable polarization modulation characterized by SOP-independent trajectory normal vectors, enabling a single-measurement direct-calculation algorithm with an angular error below 2°. The combination of this compact deterministic LC-PC and its efficient control scheme provides a practical solution for polarization management in quantum key distribution, optical sensing, and advanced photonic systems.
summary: The paper presents a novel, compact liquid-crystal polarization controller designed to manage polarization states in photonic systems. It introduces a unique control algorithm that calculates the necessary voltage settings using only one initial state measurement. This combination offers a practical, low-loss solution for high-precision polarization management critical for quantum key distribution and optical sensing.
main_problem: Existing polarization controllers suffer from performance trade-offs, requiring complex calibration or multiple state measurements.
main_result: The authors developed a compact liquid-crystal controller with a single-measurement direct-calculation algorithm achieving high accuracy and low loss.
method: A geometric rotation synthesis approach is used to calculate required voltages directly from the initial State of Polarization (SOP) measurement, bypassing iterative optimization.
model_or_system: The system is a compact liquid-crystal polarization controller (LC-PC) implemented in a butterfly package. It models the LC cell as a voltage-controlled linear retarder whose transformation matrix governs polarization changes on the Poincaré sphere.
key_observables: Insertion loss (<1 dB), driving voltage (<6 V), angular error (<2°), and full Poincaré sphere coverage.
important_parameters: LC cell gap ($10 \mu	ext{m}$), operating wavelength ($\lambda$), and the deterministic nature of SOP-independent trajectory normal vectors.
main_assumptions: The control relies on the highly predictable, SOP-independent polarization modulation characteristic of the LC-PC structure.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the structural layout, Poincaré sphere trajectories for various input SOPs, and schematics detailing the geometric decomposition used in the single-measurement control algorithm.
paper_structure: The paper first identifies limitations in existing PCs, proposes the deterministic LC-PC, details the mathematical model and the novel single-measurement direct-calculation algorithm, validates performance through experimental measurements on the Poincaré sphere, and concludes with its application potential in QKD.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses hardware implementation challenges for quantum communication protocols (like QKD) by providing a low-loss, compact component that simplifies complex polarization management into a single measurement step.
